rows.text:

a = F_net / m

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The first law is not a special case you may skip. It tells you which frames the second law may use.  ·  Action and reaction never cancel each other, because they are drawn on two different bodies.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Smooth means friction is taken as zero.  ·  g is about 9.8 m/s^2, and 10 m/s^2 is the usual classroom estimate.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Newton's first law says a body stays at rest, or keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed, unless a net external force acts on it. A frame in which this is true is an inertial frame.  ·  The second law gives the size and direction of the effect. The net force equals the rate of change of momentum. When the mass is constant this is F_net = ma, and the acceleration points the same way as the net force.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A constant velocity does not need a forward force once friction is zero.  ·  Mass stays the same when you go to the Moon. Weight does not.

rows.text: Connection of Newton's Laws of Motion (Foundations of Dynamics) to other topics  ·  First law: zero net force means constant velocity.  ·  Second law: F_net = ma.  ·  Third law: equal and opposite forces on two bodies.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The third law says forces come in pairs. If body A pushes body B, body B pushes body A with the same magnitude and the opposite direction. The two forces act on different bodies, so they do not cancel on one free-body diagram.  ·  Mass measures inertia. For the same net force, a larger mass has a smaller acceleration. Weight is the gravitational force W = mg and is not the same quantity as mass.  ·  A free-body diagram shows only the forces acting on the body you chose. Contact forces such as the normal force and friction are drawn at the surface. The weight is drawn at the centre of gravity, downward.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Draw forces on one body only.  ·  Newton's Laws of Motion (Foundations of Dynamics) is based on fundamental principles.  ·  If the body does not accelerate vertically, the vertical forces balance.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A net force of zero means the velocity is constant, which includes staying at rest.  ·  Third-law pairs are on two bodies.  ·  Write F = ma and say what each symbol means.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  The normal force from a table and the weight of a book are not a third-law pair. The third-law partner of the book's weight is the gravitational pull of the book on the Earth.
